eng_translation: Cholecystitis is the inflammation of the gallbladder, typically caused by gallstones blocking the cystic duct, leading to infection and potential complications such as gangrene or perforation. It is often associated with right upper quadrant pain, fever, and elevated white blood cell count. Diagnosis is usually confirmed with imaging studies like ultrasound, and treatment may involve antibiotics, pain management, and surgical removal of the gallbladder (cholecystectomy) if recurrent or severe.
